findings.issue_text: Posts with cook_method: raw_html return raw verbatim and embed view renders it with raw post.cooked, allowing stored XSS from untrusted third-party feed HTML on the Discourse origin; needs sanitize before storage or render
Migration sets cook_method default to 1 which maps to raw_html in the 0-based enum, so all regular posts skip cooking and render raw markdown as HTML; default should be 0
poll_feed.rb calls CGI.unescapeHTML on feed content, converting escaped entities like <script> back into live HTML before storage and raw rendering, enabling XSS injection

poll_feed.rb calls i.content.scrub which raises NoMethodError on nil content for Atom feeds without a content element; combined with retry: false the entire hourly poll silently stops and later items are never imported

TopicRetriever uses non-atomic $redis.setnx followed by $redis.expire; if the process dies between calls the key persists forever with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed URL; use SET key val EX 60 NX

Missing test coverage: no test asserting regular posts (cook_method default) are cooked through the normal pipeline, no tests for PollFeed#poll_feed parsing (nil content, missing link/id), and no tests for the redis throttle in TopicRetriever

feed_key is computed but never used in poll_feed.rb, so the job fetches and iterates the entire feed every hour doing a DB query + SHA1 per item even when nothing changed; also open() is called with no timeout so a hung feed server blocks the scheduled job

embed.js uses discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 for substring matching instead of strict equality (e.origin !== discourseUrl or comparing parsed hosts), a message-validation anti-pattern that can admit unexpected senders

TopicEmbed#import mutates the caller's contents string in place, and url =~ /^https?\:\/\// accepts degenerate URLs like 'http://' causing URI::InvalidURIError in absolutize_urls, crashing the importing job instead of rejecting the URL
The loading page unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds; if retrieval permanently fails (e.g. user doesn't exist or remote fetch errors), the iframe reloads forever with no error state

The category option in disqus.thor was silently removed, breaking existing users/scripts invoking thor disqus:import -c and causing imported threads to no longer land in a category; keep the option or document the breaking change

Modifying the already-shipped create_top_topics migration to add force: true (which drops the table if it exists) is dangerous; re-running migrations against an environment with data in top_topics would destroy it

Concurrent first-time embed requests for the same URL each enqueue a retrieve_topic job; the exists? check in TopicRetriever races with TopicEmbed.create!, so a duplicate insert can hit the unique index and raise, failing the job after a topic was already created; should rescue/handle the uniqueness violation

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Posts with cook_method: raw_html return raw verbatim and embed view renders it with raw post.cooked, allowing stored XSS from untrusted third-party feed HTML on the Discourse origin; needs sanitize before storage or render

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `cook_method` that allows skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` using HTML content pulled from third-party sources (RSS via `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and remote pages via `open(url).read` + `ruby-readability`), with no sanitization step shown before storage. The embed view then renders `post.cooked` using `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which for `raw_html` equals the unescaped third-party HTML. This is a verifiable stored XSS risk on the Discourse origin (the embedded iframe content is served from Discourse and executes in that origin).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration sets cook_method default to 1 which maps to raw_html in the 0-based enum, so all regular posts skip cooking and render raw markdown as HTML; default should be 0

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. In Discourse/Rails codebases using this `Enum` helper, values are 1-based (first symbol maps to 1, next to 2, etc.), not 0-based. The migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` therefore sets the default to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. Additionally, raw HTML skipping is explicitly gated by `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so only posts created with that cook_method (e.g., via `TopicEmbed.import` passing `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`) will bypass cooking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb calls CGI.unescapeHTML on feed content, converting escaped entities like <script> back into live HTML before storage and raw rendering, enabling XSS injection

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In Jobs::PollFeed, feed item content is taken from `i.content`, then `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` explicitly converts escaped entities (e.g., `<script>`) back into literal HTML. That content is passed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. The diff also changes `Post#cook` to return `raw` directly for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Finally, the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This combination makes it a verifiable XSS vector if the polled feed content contains malicious HTML/JS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb calls i.content.scrub which raises NoMethodError on nil content for Atom feeds without a content element; combined with retry: false the entire hourly poll silently stops and later items are never imported
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that `i.content.scrub` assumes `i.content` is present, but some feeds (RSS/Atom) omit the `content` element/field, causing a `NoMethodError` on nil. adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever uses non-atomic $redis.setnx followed by $redis.expire; if the process dies between calls the key persists forever with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed URL; use SET key val EX 60 NX

adjudication.rationale:
In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle is implemented as:
- if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
    $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
    return false
  end
This is a two-step, non-atomic pattern. If the process crashes or is killed after setnx succeeds but before expire runs, the key is left without a TTL, causing retrieved_recently? to return true forever for that embed_url (since subsequent setnx calls will fail), permanently preventing retrieval for that URL. This defect is directly present in the diff and the suggested atomic SET ... NX EX approach would avoid it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage: no test asserting regular posts (cook_method default) are cooked through the normal pipeline, no tests for PollFeed#poll_feed parsing (nil content, missing link/id), and no tests for the redis throttle in TopicRetriever

adjudication.rationale: The finding is essentially a test-coverage request. From the diff we can see some new specs were added (e.g., TopicRetriever and PollFeed#execute preconditions), and it’s true the diff does not add tests that exercise PollFeed#poll_feed parsing details or the real Redis throttling behavior. However, the claim that there is “no test” for default/regular cooking or these behaviors across the codebase is not verifiable from the diff alone (tests could already exist elsewhere), and lack of additional tests is not itself a concrete bug/correctness defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key is computed but never used in poll_feed.rb, so the job fetches and iterates the entire feed every hour doing a DB query + SHA1 per item even when nothing changed; also open() is called with no timeout so a hung feed server blocks the scheduled job

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `feed_key` is defined (SHA1 of `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) but is never referenced anywhere in the job, so it provides no caching/throttling based on feed modification. As written, `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items` every run; for each item it calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which performs at least a lookup `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and computes `Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` (plus possible updates). Also, the call to `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is made without any explicit timeout options, so the job can block on a slow/hung remote feed (it relies on library defaults rather than enforcing a bounded timeout).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed#import mutates the caller's contents string in place, and url =~ /^https?\:\/\// accepts degenerate URLs like 'http://' causing URI::InvalidURIError in absolutize_urls, crashing the importing job instead of rejecting the URL
The loading page unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds; if retrieval permanently fails (e.g. user doesn't exist or remote fetch errors), the iframe reloads forever with no error state

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic and renders 'loading'. The loading template (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb) unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds. There is no error/timeout state. Several permanent-failure paths in the diff would leave topic_id forever nil, e.g. TopicRetriever#fetch_http returns immediately if the configured embed_by_username user is missing, or remote fetching/parsing raises and the embed is never created. In those cases the iframe will keep reloading indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The category option in disqus.thor was silently removed, breaking existing users/scripts invoking thor disqus:import -c and causing imported threads to no longer land in a category; keep the option or document the breaking change

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line was removed, along with all logic that read `options[:category]` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The import path now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` without any category parameter. This is a verifiable backward-incompatible change: existing scripts invoking `thor disqus:import -c ...` will now fail due to an unknown option (or at minimum the category will no longer be applied), and imported threads will no longer be targeted to a chosen category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Modifying the already-shipped create_top_topics migration to add force: true (which drops the table if it exists) is dangerous; re-running migrations against an environment with data in top_topics would destroy it

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists when that migration is executed. However, in normal operation migrations are not re-run once applied, and for fresh installs the table won’t exist yet, so no data would be dropped. The proposed finding hinges on a hypothetical scenario (re-running/redoing this migration against an existing `top_topics` table with data or a mismatched schema_migrations state), which is not something the diff itself makes verifiably likely or introduces as a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrent first-time embed requests for the same URL each enqueue a retrieve_topic job; the exists? check in TopicRetriever races with TopicEmbed.create!, so a duplicate insert can hit the unique index and raise, failing the job after a topic was already created; should rescue/handle the uniqueness violation

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url and creates TopicEmbed rows via `TopicEmbed.create!` inside `TopicEmbed.import` after first doing `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` / `if embed.blank?`. There is no locking or rescue around this check-then-insert sequence, so two concurrent executions for the same URL can both see no row and then both attempt `create!`, causing a `RecordNotUnique`/unique-violation exception. `TopicRetriever` also has an `exists?` guard, but it’s a separate check and can race the same way, and throttling can be bypassed (`no_throttle`) or avoided via other callers (e.g., feed polling / imports). This can fail a job even after a topic/post was already created by the competing worker.
